correctness.rationale: Orthogonal spectral decomposition of the exact unnormalized Laplacian gives four explicit signed heat masses. Their signs and the graph metric reduce W1 to a two-channel transport problem with a forced cost-two imbalance. Algebra selects the larger-part branch and a single explicit Lipschitz potential achieves equality for every t. Differentiation proves the unique peak and exact size threshold. The excluded singleton case is proved separately. Matrix exponentials and independent LP checks support but do not replace these arguments.

value.rationale: The exact time-dependent Lipschitz stability of diffusion on a natural family of graph geometries is an intrinsic functional-analytic operator norm. The result detects a sharp degree-imbalance phase transition between monotonic norm contraction and transient amplification, provides the full nonasymptotic peak and common extremizer, and quantifies a dimension-free asymptotic amplification limit of two. These address the behavior beyond previously available infinitesimal curvature bounds.
